 Closings and Delays Susan Smith denied parole again, 32 years after killing sons in Upstate lake 
 Susan Smith was denied parole Thursday for a second time, more than three decades after she drowned her two young sons in an Upstate lake. By Anisa Snipes Published : Nov. 19, 2026 at 6:07 AM EST | Updated : 45 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google COLUMBIA, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - Susan Smith was denied parole Thursday for a second time, more than three decades after she drowned her two young sons in an Upstate lake.
 Smith appeared before a South Carolina parole board on Nov. 19. Her first parole hearing was in 2024, when she became eligible for parole . 
 Susan Smith addresses the board
 During Thursday’s hearing, Smith apologized for killing her sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alex.
 “I know that what I did to Michael and Alex was horrible. And I have a lot of ... I have a lot of remorse,” Smith said. “And I want to say that I’m very, very sorry. I want to say I’m sorry to Michael and Alex.”
 Smith said the boys were innocent and did not deserve to die. She also apologized to their father, David Smith, and others who knew and loved them.
 “I know that David didn’t get to see Michael and Alex grow up. He didn’t get to see him ride a bike, go to school,” she said. “And I’m really, really sorry for that. And I would go back and change all of that. If I could, I would. But I can’t.”
 Smith told the board she has changed and wants to help others.
 “I’m not the same person I was 32 years ago. I have changed. I have grown up. I have matured,” she said.
 She also denied that she killed the boys because of a man, saying, “I would never have hurt Michael and Alex for that reason.”
 Smith said that if released, she wanted to “live my life to please God and to honor the memory of Michael and Alex.”
 David Smith asks board to deny parole
 David Smith also addressed the board, asking members to deny parole and describing the pain he still carries more than three decades after his sons’ deaths.
 “I realize it’s been 32 years since I had to bury Michael and Alex. And I know that some of you, 32 years is a long time. But for me, it’s yesterday,” he said.
 David Smith said he was there to advocate for his sons.
 “And I know in my heart, granting her parole would be a huge injustice to Michael and Alex,” he said.
 He asked board members to consider his pain and “still broken heart” as they weighed whether 32 years was enough for what Susan Smith had done.
 What happened to Michael and Alex
 Smith is serving a life sentence for the 1994 murders of her sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alex. She strapped the boys into their car seats and let her car roll into John D. Long Lake in Union County.
 Smith initially claimed a man had stolen her car with the children inside, prompting a search that drew national attention. Nine days later, she confessed. Divers found the car and the boys’ bodies in the lake.
 A jury convicted Smith of murder and sentenced her to life in prison. Under the law in effect when she was sentenced, she became eligible for parole after serving 30 years.
 Ahead of Smith’s first parole hearing in 2024, the boys’ father, David Smith, told FOX Carolina he opposed her release.
 “I have been dreading this year for almost 30 years,” he said at the time. “That would be a total injustice if she was to get out … that wouldn’t be any justice to Michael and Alex. They didn’t do anything to her, and she took their lives from them.”
